newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Jet-propelled Brussels bourse heads heavenwards.
newsitem.headline: Jet-propelled Brussels bourse heads heavenwards.

text.p: Signs of accelerating economic growth, low interest rates and the booming Dow combined to propel the Brussels bourse to new record highs on Monday despite some uncertainty over the European Union's single currency plan.

But traders noted that volume was fairly thin and it was more that players were hanging onto the tail of the tiger than they had real confidence the rally that has lifted the bourse 25 percent this year was limitless.
"If all goes well with the stability pact and interest rates keep coming down then there is no reason we won't keep moving higher," one traded said.
"However, we are now very expensive. It is difficult to find things to buy. I am a bit worried, but this is not a market to go short in," he added.
The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares ended a buoyant Monday up 1.29 percent at a new closing high of 2,339.64, having earlier hit a new intra-day high of 2,342.97.

Main gainer of the day was Kredietbank, up 5.2 percent to 16,075 francs with 14,000 shares traded on renewed speculation of its involvement in strategic alliances with Belgium's CERA Bank or the Netherlands' Rabobank to create a Benelux banking structure, traders said.

Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere, which rose more than 12 percent last week, was again stronger, rising 2.7 percent to 3,285 francs as institutions placed large buy orders due to reemerging interest in the formerly ailing firm.
Construction industry firms CBR and Koramic also performed well as investors switched their attention into cyclical stocks, traders said.
CBR was up 2.2 percent to 3,435 francs, while Koramic rose 2.8 percent to 2,215 francs.
Holding company Gevaert likewise rose three percent to 3,255 francs.
Traders said the rise could have been linked with the forthcoming change in ownership of the company between Almanij and Cobepa.
In this context they noted there had been a large coss trade in Almanij, which ended 2.0 percent up at 16,500.
Chemical firm Solvay was another strong performer, rising 1.8 percent to 22,750 francs. Traders said this was largely due to a delayed reaction to positive comments last week.
Oil major PetroFina rose 0.6 percent to 12,550 francs.

Traders said the rise was mainly due to players who had sold shares based on last week's warrant expiry having to buy them back again with the fortnightly account ending on Tuesday but the new shares unlikely to be available before the end of the month.
